title: Companies, Monoliths, and Government
text: Zenith is governed by 24 Monoliths– corporations that have grown powerful enough to effectively become governments. Each Monolith controls one or more Zones, along with a major industry. A Monolith controls the laws, infrastructure, resources, and services within its territory while also running its industry across Zenith. The 24 Monoliths together form The Conglomerate, which handles things that affect Zenith as a whole. CORPORATIONS Corporations make up the vast majority of Zenith's economy. They own businesses and property, employ people, provide goods and services, and compete with one another for just about everything worth having. Corporations operate with a considerable amount of freedom and independence average citizens do not have. But despite their power and ever-looming presence, Only Monoliths can have sovereignty over a Zone. Corporate conflicts are common. Companies may compete over resources, territory, contracts, technology, or influence. These conflicts can range from economic pressure and espionage to sabotage and even full on armed conflict. Most of the time, Monoliths leave corporations to deal with their own disputes, But they may step in if a conflict starts threatening infrastructure or their own interests. MONOLITHS A Monolith is a corporation that has become dominant enough to control an entire industry. There are 24 Monoliths in Zenith, each associated with a major industry. Their influence extends far beyond their base Zones, and most businesses operating within their industries ultimately have to deal with them. BioMedica, for example, is the health Monolith. Hospitals, pharmaceuticals, medical research, and other major medical services fall under its influence. Monoliths can license their technology and services to other companies, meaning not every business associated with a Monolith is directly owned by it. These companies are still expected to operate within the Monolith's rules. GOVERNING A ZONE Every Monolith has a base Zone where its government is located. Some Monoliths control more than one Zone. A Zone is, for all practical purposes, a country. Its Monolith controls the laws, taxes, infrastructure, public services, transportation, resources, and borders of the territory, etc. Most of these things are handled locally, meaning life can look very different from one Zone to another. A Monolith administers its Zone through its own government departments and officials. The Monolith's CEO ultimately holds authority over both the corporation and its government. Owning land does not make a company a Monolith. The important difference is sovereignty. A corporation can own property within a Zone, but the Monolith decides what happens within the Zone itself. BECOMING A MONOLITH In theory, any corporation can become a Monolith. In practice, this means becoming powerful enough to dominate an industry and taking control of a Zone. Usually, this requires displacing an existing Monolith. This is extremely rare. Monoliths can remain in power for centuries, and replacing one is a major event for all of Zenith. THE CONGLOMERATE The Conglomerate is the closest thing Zenith has to a central government. All 24 Monoliths are members, and each has one vote. A Monolith's population, wealth, or number of Zones does not give it additional voting power. The Conglomerate handles matters that affect multiple Zones, maintains shared institutions, and establishes the relatively small number of laws that apply throughout Zenith. It does not directly govern individual Zones. A Monolith is still free to run its own territory, and The Conglomerate cannot simply replace a Monolith's leadership or take control of one of its Zones. CONGLOMERATE LAWS Most laws in Zenith are decided at the Zone level. Criminal law, taxation, business regulations, licensing, and many other rules can vary from one Zone to another. Conglomerate law mainly covers matters that affect Zenith as a whole and rules that keep the Monoliths from completely tearing each other apart. Some of the most important Conglomerate laws include: Murder is prohibited. Theft is prohibited. Monoliths must respect each other's territorial sovereignty. No Monolith may claim or annex another Monolith's Zone. Conglomerate Institutions must be recognized throughout Zenith. Monoliths must abide by decisions made through the Conglomerate's voting process. These laws, despite being universal, aren't enforced very well. Enforcement varies between Zones, and Monoliths are can and will interfere with law enforcement when it suits them. INSTITUTIONS The Institutions are organizations maintained by The Conglomerate that operate across the Zones. Some of the more familiar ones are: The Gavel: Law enforcement. The Scale: Courts and the judicial system. The Ledger: Taxes and Conglomerate finances. The Registry: Legal and civil records. The Arm: Major disasters and emergencies. The Institutions are supposed to operate throughout Zenith, but they still have to work within territory controlled by a Monolith. A local branch can therefore find itself restricted or interfered with by the government of the Zone it operates in. For most people, dealing with an Institution can feel very different depending on where they are. RELATIONS BETWEEN MONOLITHS The Monoliths are competitors, but they can't afford to completely ignore one another. Every Zone depends on things produced somewhere else. Food might come from one Zone, medicine from another, and transportation may be controlled by a third. Keeping all of this moving requires the Monoliths to cooperate, even when they don't particularly like each other. They still get in each other's way. A Monolith might try to undercut another company's business, interfere with its operations, or gain an advantage through the Conglomerate. Things can get considerably worse when their interests directly collide. Open warfare is uncommon. A fight between two Monoliths could disrupt entire industries and affect millions of people, so there is usually a reason to find another way. For the average person, the Monoliths are simply the powers that run Zenith. Which one you live under determines a surprising amount about your life.Usually.

title: Fixers
description: Dont wanna be a Corpo? Look no further!
text: Fixers are independent contractors hired to do jobs that someone else can't, won't, or doesn't want to deal with themselves. Fixers can work for pretty much anyone. Private citizens, businesses, Corporations, and even Monoliths will hire them when they need something done without putting their own people on the job. A Fixer's work can be completely legal, highly illegal, or somewhere in between depending on who's paying and where the job takes place. Most Fixers work for themselves and take jobs one at a time, although some form long-term partnerships or work as part of a larger group, known a Network. Common Fixer Jobs There's no real limit to what a Fixer can be hired to do. Some specialize in a particular kind of work, while others will take whatever pays. Some examples are, but not limited to: Couriers: Delivering packages, messages, or people. Runners: Moving illegal or restricted cargo between Zones, often through the Pale. Guards: Protecting people, property, or important cargo. Hunters: Tracking down wanted or missing people. Ghosts: Finding information, uncovering secrets, or locating people who don't want to be found. Saboteurs: Disrupting businesses, damaging property, or getting in the way of a competitor. Cleaners: Getting rid of specific targets, usually for criminal or political clients. Mechanics: Repairing equipment, modifying technology, or dealing with systems other people can't figure out. Admins: Handling paperwork, finances, taxes, and other boring problems. FIXER NETWORKS Fixers don't always work alone. Many belong to Fixer Networks, loose organizations of Fixers who share contacts, resources, and jobs. Networks can be small groups of friends or large organizations with members spread across multiple Zones. Some are highly organized, with offices, rankings, and their own job boards, while others are little more than a and a list of people to call when a job comes up. Being part of a Network can make finding work much easier. A Fixer might take a job through their Network, pass it along to someone better suited for it, or call on another member when they need help. There's no single way to run a Network. Some are little more than professional associations, while others operate almost like guilds with their own rules, reputation, and internal hierarchy. Due to some Networks being officially recognized as Corporations, they are granted a lot more leniency with the law then a freelance or low grade fixer.

title: Signatures
text: SIGNATURES Signatures are rare 'living' weapons created from the cores of an old, powerful extinct species known as Moon Children. Each Signature possesses its own abilities and can form a permanent bond with a compatible human. A person bonded to a Signature is called a Signer. Due to its history, Signatures are wildly known to exist, but they are still extremely uncommon. Most people will never encounter one. Due to the Extinction of Moon Children in year 320, no more Signatures are capable of being created. THE BOND A Signature can only be wielded by someone it bonds with. What makes someone compatible isn't fully understood, although personality, experiences, and temperament seem to play a role. Once bonded, the human becomes a Signer. The Signature will refuse to work for anyone else, and its appearance may gradually change as its relationship with its Signer develops. The bond also gives Signers physical abilities beyond those of ordinary humans, such as increased strength, speed, endurance, and resilience. ABILITIES Every Signature has its own unique ability or set of related abilities. A Signer usually learns the most obvious uses first, with more advanced applications developing through experience and experimentation. No two Signatures are necessarily alike, and their abilities can vary dramatically. DISTORTIONS A Distortion occurs when the bond between a Signer and their Signature becomes severely destabilized. This can happen while a Signer is alive, usually during extreme emotional distress. The Signature begins to merge with its Signer, gradually taking control of their body and actions. Early stages can sometimes be reversed, but advanced Distortions are increasingly difficult to recover from. Death can also result in a Distortion under certain circumstances. A Signer who dies peacefully, such as from illness or old age, will generally leave their Signature unbound, allowing it to eventually choose another compatible person. Violent death or death accompanied by intense unresolved attachment may instead cause the Signature to attempt to preserve its bond. In these cases, a complete Distortion may form. A complete Distortion is no longer the original signer, and its final appearance will often resemble the Moon Child's former self. SIGNERS There are very few active Signers across Zenith. Some openly use their Signatures, while others keep them hidden to avoid attention from Monoliths and other Fixers, or anyone else interested in their abilities.

title: The Pale
text: The Pale is the name commonly given to the regions outside the Zones. It is not a single biome or uniformly barren wasteland, but a vast collection of natural environments ranging from relatively ordinary wilderness to extremely harsh and dense regions. Parts of the Pale can look surprisingly similar to the edges of nearby Zones. The difference becomes more apparent with distance, where larger expanses of wilderness, denser vegetation, unfamiliar wildlife, and other features of Zenith's native environment become increasingly common. The Pale can be extraordinarily beautiful, But is nevertheless dangerous for most unprepared and ordinary humans due to the of environmental conditions and biological hazards. Most Zenithans regard the Pale as inherently dangerous and unsuitable for permanent human habitation, the name itself even carrying negative connotations. For more information on Zenith, Refer to it's page.

title: Zenith
text: OVERVIEW Zenith is the planet humanity settled after abandoning Earth nearly 1,000 years ago. The planet is significantly different from Earth, with its own plants, animals, ecosystems, and geological processes. Humanity has spent centuries studying Zenith, but the majority of the planet's aspects remain barely understood. Most of humanity lives within one of the 24 Zones, heavily developed regions controlled by the Monoliths. Outside the Zones lies the Pale, where conditions are much harder for humans to live in. GEOGRAPHY & LIFE While appearing on the surface very similar to earth, Zenith is a strange and diverse planet, with many biomes and ecosystems having no direct Earth equivalent. Some species are harmless and live alongside humans, while others can be dangerous to people and infrastructure. Large portions of the planet remain sparsely explored, particularly outside developed areas. THE ZONES The 24 Zones are the main centers of human civilization on Zenith. Each is governed by a Monolith, which controls its government, infrastructure, and major industries. Zones are heavily managed environments designed to keep their populations safe and comfortable. Each Zone is surrounded by a largely invisible barrier that helps maintain its conditions and limits the movement of contaminants and other environmental factors. THE PALE The Pale refers to the area outside of zones. Refer to the page on The Pale to learn more.

title: AquaFlo
description: The Monolith responsible for water extraction, purification, and distribution throughout Zenith.
text: OVERVIEW The water of Zenith is mildly toxic. It can be safely consumed for short periods, but long-term exposure causes a variety of health problems and can significantly reduce a person's lifespan. AquaFlo is the Monolith responsible for extracting, purifying, and distributing water across Zenith. Its infrastructure includes wells, treatment plants, pipelines, reservoirs, and countless smaller facilities scattered throughout the Zones and Pale. AquaFlo is particularly prominent in Rho, where centuries of water extraction have made the company a major part of the Zone's economy and development. HISTORY AquaFlo was established during the formation of the modern Zones, originally to deal with Zenith's contaminated water. Its early infrastructure was concentrated in what would become Rho, where the company quickly became responsible for much of the region's water supply. As AquaFlo expanded its extraction sites, purification plants, pipelines, and reservoirs, its control over Rho's water infrastructure eventually allowed it to become the Zone's Monolith. The company continued expanding across Zenith over the following centuries. Some of its older water sources have since been exhausted, leaving abandoned facilities scattered throughout Rho. Many have been salvaged or repurposed by locals, while others remain under AquaFlo ownership. AquaFlo's leadership has remained within the same family for generations. STRUCTURE AquaFlo is headed by the CEO, historically titled Lord/Lady [NAME], the Great Purifier of the Waters. The full title still appears on official documents, although most people simply call them the CEO. The position traditionally passes to the CEO's firstborn child. The ruling family occupies an unusually privileged position within the company, with wealthy AquaFlo families and senior management forming a loose corporate upper class beneath them. Most employees occupy much more ordinary positions. AquaFlo employs large numbers of workers across its infrastructure, including: Researchers and Hydrologists: Study water sources and purification methods. Engineers: Design and maintain AquaFlo's infrastructure and equipment. Factory Workers: Operate treatment plants and other industrial facilities. Maintenance Workers: Repair pipes, machinery, pumps, and other equipment. Surveyors and Field Workers: Locate and assess potential water sources. Security: Protect AquaFlo facilities, workers, and valuable infrastructure. Management: Oversee individual facilities, districts, and larger operations. CULTURE AquaFlo has a strong sense of hierarchy. The company's ruling family is treated with considerably more respect and ceremony than ordinary employees, and differences in wealth and living conditions are obvious. The company takes considerable pride in its history and presents water management as a responsibility passed down through generations. Many employees genuinely take pride in keeping their communities supplied with clean water, while others are simply there for the stable employment and benefits. Working conditions vary depending on the job. Office positions and specialized careers can be comfortable, while factory, maintenance, and field work can be physically demanding and dangerous. AquaFlo employees often develop strong camaraderie, particularly among workers who spend long periods together at remote facilities or company towns. RELATIONSHIPS Other Monoliths AquaFlo is not always easy to work with. Its search for new water sources occasionally brings it into other Monoliths' territory, and its leadership has a reputation for being abrasive. Despite this, AquaFlo is too important to easily oppose. Nearly every Zone depends on its infrastructure in some capacity, and major disruptions to the water supply could affect thousands or millions of people. Rho Rho has been shaped by centuries of AquaFlo extraction. Water shortages, dried vegetation, and depleted sources are common concerns in parts of the Zone, particularly around older extraction sites. AquaFlo controls most of Rho's major water infrastructure, although independent wells, purification systems, and smaller suppliers still exist. When a water source is no longer worth operating, AquaFlo generally abandons the facility and moves elsewhere. Equipment may be salvaged, but the structures themselves are often left behind. Rhoans frequently repurpose these abandoned facilities as workshops, storage buildings, homes, or sources of spare parts. AquaFlo usually ignores this unless someone interferes with valuable equipment or an active system. The Talora AquaFlo and the Talora have a particularly hostile relationship. AquaFlo operations have repeatedly displaced Talora communities and restricted their access to areas surrounding company infrastructure. Talora are generally not permitted to work for AquaFlo or enter company property. Stories of more extreme actions by AquaFlo are common, although many of these remain difficult to verify. WORKING FOR AQUAFLO AquaFlo employs people across nearly every level of its operations, making it possible to build very different kinds of characters around the company. A character might work at a purification plant, maintain pipelines in a company town, or provide security for an isolated facility. More interestingly, many employees are being forced to set up shop and survey The Pale for water sources. Working in the Pale is dangerous, but positions may come with better pay or benefits. Some employees spend years moving between facilities as the company follows new water sources. NOTES AquaFlo is one of the oldest continuously operating Monoliths. It is one of the most geographically spread-out Monoliths, with facilities throughout the Zones and Pale. AquaFlo infrastructure can remain operational for generations, with newer systems often built around older facilities. Many Rho settlements originally developed around AquaFlo infrastructure. Abandoned AquaFlo facilities are common sights throughout Rho.

title: BioMedica
description: Zenith's largest healthcare corporation and the Monolith responsible for Lamda.
text: OVERVIEW BioMedica is Zenith's largest healthcare corporation and the Monolith responsible for Lamda. Its operations include hospitals, clinics, medical research, healthcare plans, and the manufacture of medical products. BioMedica is known for its medical services and the effectiveness of its treatments. Its hospitals are well-funded, and its research has produced significant medical advancements. The corporation also manufactures a wide range of medical products, including Healing Foam, a popular treatment among Fixers despite its high price. Healthcare plans are available at varying levels of cost and coverage. Monolith employees commonly receive healthcare benefits through their employment, making corporate positions particularly attractive. However, coverage can be expensive for lower-income individuals, and uninsured patients face substantially higher costs. BioMedica employs an enormous workforce across its medical, research, manufacturing, administrative, and corporate divisions. Its services are used throughout Zenith, and it maintains business relationships with the other Monoliths. HISTORY BioMedica grew through its success in healthcare and medical research. Its hospitals, treatments, and medical products established its reputation, while its services became increasingly important to the other Monoliths. As more Monoliths began offering BioMedica healthcare plans as an employee benefit, the corporation gained a broad customer base and lasting business relationships. Healthcare coverage became a common employment benefit across corporate Zenith. Its growing resources supported further research and development, allowing BioMedica to expand its medical capabilities and operations throughout the Zones. The corporation eventually became the dominant force in healthcare on Zenith. Lamda developed around BioMedica's medical facilities, research institutions, corporate offices, and residential communities. It now serves as the corporation's primary base and a major center for medical professionals, researchers, and retirees. STRUCTURE BioMedica's operations are divided across several major branches: Medical Services: Hospitals, clinics, doctors, and other healthcare facilities. Healthcare Plans: Programs that cover medical expenses for individuals and corporate employees. Research and Development: Medical research and the development of treatments, technologies, and products. Manufacturing: Production of pharmaceuticals, medical equipment, Healing Foam, and other healthcare products. Administration: Corporate management, personnel, logistics, and coordination between divisions. Headquarters establishes company-wide policies and allocates resources across its operations. Medical facilities and manufacturing divisions follow standardized procedures, while research teams develop new treatments and technologies. CULTURE BioMedica maintains a professional, clinical, and research-oriented workplace culture. Employees are expected to meet high standards and maintain the corporation's reputation for medical competence. Employment is considered prestigious, particularly for doctors, senior researchers, and other highly qualified professionals. These positions can offer strong compensation, healthcare benefits, and opportunities for advancement. Working conditions vary by position. Senior medical staff and experienced researchers generally receive better compensation and professional status, while junior researchers and support staff face more ordinary corporate conditions. Advancement is closely tied to performance and seniority. Many employees take pride in their work and regard medical research as an important contribution to human health. The corporation's demanding standards and competitive research environment are characteristic of its workplace. RELATIONSHIPS Other Monoliths BioMedica maintains cooperative relationships with the other Monoliths by providing healthcare plans, medical services, and products for their employees. These arrangements benefit both parties. Other Monoliths can offer healthcare as an employment benefit, while BioMedica gains a broad customer base and reliable business relationships. The corporation generally avoids unnecessary conflict over ordinary medical matters. It does, however, closely protect its proprietary treatments, research methods, and medical technology. The Public BioMedica is generally regarded as one of the more respectable Monoliths. Its hospitals and treatments are widely used, and its research has produced genuine medical advancements. Public criticism primarily concerns the cost of healthcare and the difficulty of obtaining adequate coverage without a well-paying job or employer-sponsored benefits. Despite these concerns, BioMedica's services remain essential throughout Zenith, and its public reputation is comparatively strong. Independent Healthcare Providers Independent doctors, clinics, and pharmacies continue to operate throughout Zenith. However, BioMedica's resources and extensive medical network make it difficult for smaller providers to compete with the corporation's reach. NOTES BioMedica is the Monolith responsible for Lamda. It is considered one of the most developed Monoliths on Zenith. Its healthcare services and research contribute to its comparatively positive public reputation. Healing Foam is one of its best-known medical products and is commonly used by Fixers. Healthcare plans are a common employment benefit across the Monoliths. BioMedica employs people across medical care, research, manufacturing, administration, and support services.

title: Palisade
description: The Monolith responsible for defense manufacturing and security infrastructure across Zenith.
text: OVERVIEW Palisade is the Monolith responsible for defense and security infrastructure across Zenith. It manufactures and supplies weapons, Gavel equipment, surveillance systems, alarms, communications equipment, and other security products used throughout the Zones. Palisade works closely with other Monoliths and corporations, providing the equipment and expertise needed to secure their territories, facilities, and operations. Its products are known for their quality, and its services remain widely used despite its reputation for brutality. The company believes that a stable society requires strict laws, effective enforcement, and the suppression of threats before they can cause widespread harm. Palisade's approach to security is exceptionally harsh, and its methods are often considered excessive or cruel. The company prioritizes results over public approval, pointing to low crime rates in areas under its protection as evidence of its effectiveness. Palisade's public image reflects its institutional identity: sleek, severe, and authoritative. Its visual branding uses silver and black with cyan accents, emphasizing precision, control, and strength. HISTORY Palisade's history in Eta began with its corporate war against Plastigen, the former Monolith controlling the Zone. Plastigen manufactured plastics using technology that had fallen behind newer materials and manufacturing techniques. Despite its environmentally destructive industry, it maintained relatively permissive laws and generally avoided interfering with private life. Eta developed a distinctive culture centered around nightlife, entertainment, recreational drugs, unusual fashion, and eccentric subcultures. Approximately thirty years ago, Palisade defeated Plastigen and seized control of Eta. Plastigen was dissolved, and its employees were killed. Palisade concealed the killings and presented the takeover as the removal of problematic elements from the Zone. Following the takeover, Palisade restructured Eta around its defense and security industries. Former Plastigen factories, warehouses, offices, utilities, and transportation facilities were repurposed, while other areas were demolished or rebuilt. The economic disruption caused widespread unemployment and displacement. Resistance began within months. Protests, strikes, and civil disobedience escalated into an extended urban uprising known as the Eta Revolt. Palisade killed and imprisoned large numbers of people while suppressing the revolt. Although the major uprising eventually ended, resistance continued through smaller underground movements, some of which developed into smuggling networks, organized crime groups, and underground nightlife syndicates. In the following decades, Palisade encouraged wealthy residents, skilled workers, and tourists to return to Eta. Redevelopment revitalized parts of the Zone but also raised living costs and displaced poorer residents. Security infrastructure became increasingly prominent, particularly in public spaces and entertainment districts. STRUCTURE Palisade operates as both a defense manufacturer and a security provider. Its products and services are used by other Monoliths, corporations, and the Gavel, giving the company a presence throughout Zenith. Its operations include: Weapons and military equipment: Manufacturing and supplying weapons and other defense products. Gavel supplies: Producing police uniforms, equipment, and other law-enforcement supplies. Surveillance systems: Manufacturing security cameras, monitoring equipment, and related technology. Alarms and communications: Providing warning systems, security communications, and monitoring infrastructure. Security infrastructure: Establishing and maintaining systems for public spaces, commercial districts, corporate facilities, and other controlled areas. Palisade also works directly with other organizations to develop and maintain their security systems. Its expertise makes it a valuable partner to companies and Monoliths that rely on external providers for their defense infrastructure. CULTURE Palisade's institutional culture emphasizes discipline, effectiveness, and authority. Employees are expected to take security seriously, follow established procedures, and prioritize the organization's objectives. The company values results over public approval. Its position is that strict enforcement is necessary to maintain a functioning society, and that the effectiveness of a security measure matters more than whether it is considered excessive. Although individual employees may take pleasure in cruelty, Palisade's institutional justification for harsh methods is primarily practical: they are acceptable if they achieve the desired outcome. Working for Palisade is closely associated with the defense and security industries. Its employees may work in manufacturing, engineering, surveillance, communications, logistics, security infrastructure, or administrative roles. The company's broad network of contracts creates demand for both technical specialists and industrial workers. Palisade's branding reinforces its values. Silver and black designs, cyan accents, angular forms, and a stern visual presentation are used to convey precision, control, and authority. RELATIONSHIPS Other Monoliths Palisade maintains generally cooperative relationships with the other Monoliths. Its weapons, surveillance equipment, and security infrastructure are valuable to organizations responsible for protecting their own territories and operations. Other Monoliths may disagree with Palisade's methods or distrust its ideology, but its effectiveness gives them practical reasons to maintain their relationships with the company. Palisade is not universally trusted, yet its products and services are too useful for most Monoliths to disregard. The Gavel Palisade manufactures and supplies equipment used by the Gavel, including uniforms, weapons, and other police supplies. Its products form part of the equipment used by law enforcement throughout Zenith. The Public Public opinion of Palisade varies between Zones. Some people appreciate the effectiveness of its security systems and consider strict enforcement a necessary trade-off for public safety. Others distrust its brutality, extensive surveillance, and willingness to impose its own standards of acceptable behavior. Palisade justifies its methods by pointing to the low crime rates of areas under its protection. It portrays criminals as threats to ordinary people and argues that objections to strict enforcement place personal freedom above public safety. Eta Palisade remains deeply unpopular among many Etans. The destruction of Plastigen, the killing of its employees, and the violent suppression of the Eta Revolt left a lasting legacy of resentment. Restrictions on nightlife and public behavior have further alienated residents who remember Eta's earlier culture. Elements of pre-Palisade Eta survive through fashion, music, nightlife, and underground venues. The slang term Brightside, a sarcastic reference to Palisade's sanitized image of the Zone, reflects local hostility toward the company's attempts to regulate and rebrand Eta. NOTES Palisade is the defense and security Monolith, supplying weapons, surveillance systems, police equipment, and security infrastructure throughout Zenith. Its products are widely relied upon despite its reputation for brutality. Eta was formerly controlled by Plastigen, a plastics manufacturer, before Palisade seized control approximately thirty years ago. The Eta Revolt was a major uprising against Palisade's rule. Its suppression remains a source of local resentment. Palisade's security philosophy prioritizes effective enforcement and the prevention of threats over public approval. The company's silver, black, and cyan branding reflects its stern, authoritative image.

title: Lamda
description: An affluent, carefully maintained Zone known for its garden cities and Art Deco-inspired architecture.
text: OVERVIEW Lamda is a densely populated Zone owned and operated by BioMedica. It is known for its carefully maintained cities, extensive greenery, Art Deco-inspired architecture, and high standard of living. The Zone is home to medical professionals, researchers, corporate employees, retirees, and wealthy residents, alongside the service workers who keep its cities running. Lamda has a reputation for being comfortable, expensive, sheltered, and somewhat snobbish. Healthcare is highly accessible throughout the Zone, and BioMedica's influence extends into much of everyday life. Its residents benefit from reliable public services and well-maintained surroundings, though this comfort comes with a distinctly corporate atmosphere. GEOGRAPHY & INFRASTRUCTURE Lamda is a relatively mild, rainy Zone with a naturally green landscape. Most developed areas consist of cities and surrounding residential neighborhoods, with gardens, parks, and landscaped streets incorporated throughout. Much of modern Lamda was constructed or redesigned by BioMedica after the collapse of the previous Monolith. The resulting cities follow a planned garden-city layout, with pedestrian-friendly streets, plazas, courtyards, and covered walkways. Architecture combines Art Deco-inspired design with futuristic materials and construction. Older and wealthier areas tend to be more ornate, while newer buildings are generally cleaner and more restrained. Cars and buses are available, but walking is a common way to get around. Public facilities are regularly maintained, and security cameras and other monitoring systems are widespread, usually blending into the surrounding architecture. HISTORY This section is not required reading, and is mainly here for those curious. Lamda was once a relatively ordinary green region whose economy relied heavily on agriculture, particularly vegetable production. Its former Monolith specialized in growing and distributing vegetables, but gradually lost ground as the Food Monolith's mushroom-based production displaced traditional agricultural supply chains. Following a major corporate crisis, the vegetable Monolith became defunct. BioMedica acquired the Zone and began a major redevelopment of its cities, turning Lamda into a headquarters and residential center for doctors, researchers, executives, and other skilled professionals. As BioMedica expanded its retirement services, Lamda also became a major destination for retirees from across Zenith. Retirement communities and elderly care are now important parts of the Zone's population and economy. CULTURE Lamdan culture places considerable value on education, professional achievement, organized social life, and comfortable living. Residents are commonly stereotyped as polite, sheltered, health-conscious, and out of touch with life in poorer Zones. Lamda also has a reputation for being humorless, although its humor tends to be dry, understated, and sarcastic. Professional competence carries considerable prestige. Doctors, researchers, engineers, academics, and other skilled workers are generally respected, and career or academic achievements can be a source of personal and family pride. Clubs, societies, and neighborhood organizations are popular ways to socialize. Many residents belong to several groups at once, ranging from professional associations to hobby clubs and recreational societies. Fashion Lamdan fashion tends to be affluent, professional, and coordinated. Tailored coats, trousers, dresses, knitwear, polished shoes, and understated accessories are common. Art Deco influences appear in geometric patterns, jewelry, and formal clothing. Expensive or well-made garments often signal social standing without relying on particularly flashy designs. Food & Dining Restaurants, cafes, bakeries, and other dining establishments are central to Lamdan social life. Bread, pastries, soups, sausages, and baked dishes are common, alongside more elaborate local and international cuisine. Health-conscious food and specialized diets are also popular, reflecting BioMedica's influence, although Lamdan cuisine is not exclusively focused on health. Going out to eat is a common way to socialize. Cafes and restaurants are used for dates, meetings, family gatherings, and casual time with friends. Music & Recreation Lamda has a strong classical and orchestral music tradition. Concerts, chamber performances, and formal musical events are common, while jazz, lounge music, piano performances, and acoustic acts are often heard in cafes and restaurants. Organized hobbies are popular throughout the Zone. Gardening, crafts, book groups, music societies, and recreational clubs provide regular social outlets. Retirement communities contribute heavily to this culture, with many activities originally associated with older residents becoming popular across the wider population. Chess is also well established in Lamda, which occasionally hosts notable competitions and has helped give the Zone a reputation for the game. Events & Festivals Garden shows, seasonal festivals, markets, charity events, and neighborhood gatherings are common throughout the year. Retirement communities hold their own dances, games, and hobby events, some of which have become wider Lamdan traditions. BioMedica also hosts medical conventions, research showcases, and corporate celebrations that attract visitors from other Zones. Local Speech Lamdan speech is generally considered close to standard Zenithan, though residents have a reputation for speaking more formally and politely than people from some other Zones. Humor is often dry or understated, and sarcasm is common. Outsiders sometimes interpret this reserved style as a lack of humor. DAILY LIFE Most Lamdans live in comfortable apartment complexes or planned residential neighborhoods. Daily life often revolves around work, shopping, dining, clubs, and community activities. Commercial districts contain boutiques, department stores, markets, cafes, and restaurants. Parks and gardens are integrated into everyday life, making walks through landscaped streets and public spaces a routine part of living in the Zone. Evenings are generally quiet. Restaurants and cafes remain active, but private dinners, club meetings, and small social gatherings are more common than a particularly prominent nightlife scene. Healthcare and public amenities are reliable. Bathrooms, water fountains, hydration stations, covered walkways, and other municipal facilities are generally well maintained. Lamda is relatively affluent, and residents often have more opportunities to move between jobs, pursue education, and access services than people in poorer Zones. BioMedica employees and retirees may have particular reasons to remain in the Zone for long periods. SUBZONES / DISTRICTS BioMedica District The central corporate and medical district. It contains BioMedica Headquarters, major hospitals, research facilities, corporate offices, and specialist clinics. Garden District Centered around Lamda's major public garden and botanical grounds. Parks, residential neighborhoods, cafes, and other public spaces fill the surrounding area. Retirement District A large area dedicated to retirement communities, assisted living, elderly services, and recreation. Both ordinary and luxury retirement communities can be found here. Resort District Contains hotels, resorts, spas, and vacation facilities. Tourism is a secondary part of Lamda's economy, attracting visitors interested in its gardens, healthcare, and comfortable surroundings. Residential Districts The Zone's main residential areas, consisting primarily of comfortable mid-rise apartment buildings, with larger luxury complexes in wealthier neighborhoods. Schools, restaurants, local businesses, and other services are distributed throughout. KEY LOCATIONS BioMedica Headquarters: A large corporate campus consisting of connected buildings, gardens, public spaces, and a central landmark building. Lamda Central Hospital District: The Zone's primary medical center, supported by smaller hospitals and clinics throughout Lamda. Lamda Public Garden: A large botanical garden and public park. Lamda Commercial Districts: Shopping and dining areas containing restaurants, cafes, markets, boutiques, and other businesses. Lamda Chess Venues: Clubs and competition venues used for local and inter-Zone chess events. ECONOMY BioMedica is the dominant economic force in Lamda and one of its largest employers. The local economy centers on healthcare, medicine, research, corporate administration, professional services, tourism, retail, and elderly care. Working for BioMedica can provide significant advantages, including better access to housing and the Zone's high standard of living. The company employs people in medical, research, administrative, maintenance, and service roles. Independent businesses remain common alongside BioMedica-affiliated companies. Restaurants, cafes, shops, and services catering to professionals and retirees make up a significant part of the local economy. Despite its affluence, Lamda still has lower-income residents and service workers. Class differences remain present, even if they are less visually dramatic than in poorer Zones. CRIME Crime in Lamda is relatively low, particularly violent crime. White-collar and corporate offenses, including fraud, bribery, and information theft, are more characteristic of the Zone. Organized crime and illicit Fixer activity exist but are uncommon. Incidents involving BioMedica occasionally occur, and some are alleged to have been quietly resolved. Lamda's sheltered reputation also makes its residents the subject of jokes about being easy targets for criminals from outside the Zone. CREATING A LAMDAN CHARACTER Lamda's population extends well beyond doctors and researchers. A Lamdan character might be a BioMedica employee, a retired worker from another Zone, a student, a restaurant owner, a corporate administrator, a maintenance worker, or someone employed in the tourism and service industries. Characters can come from comfortable professional households or from the lower-income communities that support the Zone's affluent lifestyle. They might take pride in Lamda's safety and amenities, feel constrained by its social expectations, or have little experience with life outside its carefully maintained cities. Someone who grew up in Lamda may be accustomed to reliable healthcare, organized social activities, and well-maintained public spaces. Leaving the Zone can expose them to living conditions and social expectations they have rarely encountered firsthand. TRIVIA Lamda's architecture draws heavily from Art Deco and garden-city design. The public garden is both a major recreational space and a botanical garden. The Zone has a large retirement population, and elderly services are an important part of its economy. Chess competitions have contributed to Lamda's association with the game. Lamdans have a reputation for being clean, polite, and somewhat humorless. The Zone's public facilities are considered among the best maintained on Zenith. Residents who move to Lamda often stay for long periods.

title: Rho
description: A massive, sparse and hot zone.
text: OVERVIEW Rho is a sparsely populated Zone ravaged by its water industry and Monolith AquaFlo. Much of the Zone consists of dry plains, red sandstone, deep canyons, and mesas. Most settlements are small and separated by long stretches of undeveloped land. Water extraction has been one of Rho's defining industries for centuries. The Zone is an important source of water for the rest of Zenith, although the wealth generated by the industry is not evenly distributed. GEOGRAPHY & INFRASTRUCTURE Rho's terrain is mostly dry and sun-baked, with sparse vegetation outside areas near settlements and reliable water sources. Large industrial facilities are scattered throughout the Zone, particularly water extraction, purification, storage, and distribution facilities. Some of these complexes are enormous, with machinery built directly into the surrounding terrain. Rho also has a large network of smaller settlements. Some are old communities that have existed for generations, while others grew around industrial facilities. HISTORY Rho's earliest human settlements were established as prisoner and slave colonies, originally used for quarrying and extracting stone and construction materials. Over generations, their descendants developed into the Talora, forming a distinct culture and identity. Water extraction eventually became Rho's dominant industry. As the industry expanded, Talora communities were gradually displaced by extraction facilities, pipelines, reservoirs, roads, and new settlements. Rho has experienced periods of prosperity because of its water industry, but much of that wealth has historically remained concentrated around the companies and communities closest to the industry. CULTURE Rho has a strong regional identity, and Rhoans generally take pride in their culture despite widespread stereotypes about the Zone. Rhoan culture is influenced by frontier traditions, Southern influences, vehicle culture, and a strong emphasis on self-sufficiency. Rhoans tend to be skeptical of outsiders, particularly people from wealthier or more urban Zones. Older technology and traditional customs are often embraced rather than discarded. Repairing, modifying, and reusing things is common, and practical skills are highly valued. Appearance Rhoans commonly have tan to medium-brown skin, brown or dark brown hair, and soft facial features with relatively broad or flat proportions. Wavy and curly hair is common, as is facial hair among adults who grow it. These traits vary considerably between individuals and are not universal among Rhoans. Fashion Rhoan clothing tends to be practical, durable, and loose-fitting, particularly because of the climate and the Zone's industrial and agricultural lifestyle. Workwear such as cargo pants, coveralls, utility vests, boots, gloves, and oversized jackets is common. Clothing is often modified with pockets, straps, tools, or other equipment. Outside of workwear, Rhoan fashion has strong streetwear and motorsport influences. Graphic jackets, racing-inspired clothing, cropped tops, loose trousers, caps, and customized garments are common. Bright colors, particularly orange, red, yellow, and blue, are popular as accents and statement pieces. Secondhand, repaired, and repurposed clothing is also widespread. Vehicle Culture Vehicles are deeply embedded in Rhoan life. The distance between settlements makes them necessary, while racing and vehicle modification are popular forms of recreation. Rho is known throughout Zenith for heavily modified vehicles, off-road racing, and unusual custom builds. Racing takes place both informally and through organized events, and major races and vehicle shows are frequently filmed in the Zone. Music Rho has a recognizable musical tradition that is considered older and more traditional than the music of many urban Zones. Its continued popularity is partly attributed to Rho's isolation and the importance placed on preserving local culture. Food & Drink Rhoan cuisine is heavily inspired by Southern American comfort food. Strong spices, sauces, rubs, and seasoning are common. Fresh ingredients and home cooking are culturally important. Depending on the settlement, gardens, livestock, hunting, and other small-scale food production may supplement imported food. Rho also has a strong culture of locally produced alcohol. Homemade drinks are often particularly strong and pungent. Sports & Festivals Dustball is a popular Rhoan sport loosely descended from soccer. Different communities maintain their own variations. The largest annual festival is the Dustrink, which combines Dustball, racing, food, music, drinking, and other local traditions. The festival is primarily community-run, and Monolith involvement has historically been limited. Local Speech Rhoan speech has its own regional slang. Longhaul: A long-distance trip, particularly between distant settlements. Tin: An old vehicle or piece of machinery. Dry luck: Bad luck or an unfortunate situation. Company town: A settlement dominated by Monolith infrastructure and employment. Pipe Rat: Someone who works around or for the water Monolith. Can also be used dismissively toward Monolith employees. Pipe Mouse: The child of a Pipe Rat, or someone who grew up around the Monolith without working for it. Dusting: Driving or riding around without a particular destination. Burnout: Someone who spends most of their money on gambling, racing, and related hobbies. Junkblood: A self-proclaimed title used by people who build, repair, or modify things from scrap. Some terms are also used against Rhoans by outsiders. Rusty, Canyon Rat, Tanker, and Outback are derogatory terms associated with stereotypes of Rhoans as poor, isolated, or backwards. DAILY LIFE Most Rhoans live in small settlements rather than large cities. Daily life generally revolves around work, family, local businesses, and community activities. Repairing vehicles, machinery, buildings, and household goods is common. Mechanics, fabricators, and other skilled tradespeople are important members of many communities. Water availability varies between settlements. Larger cities and industrial communities generally have reliable supplies, while remote communities may depend on wells, storage systems, or water deliveries. Bars, diners, garages, shops, and private homes commonly serve as gathering places. Education is generally less well-funded than in wealthier Zones. Rho has several trade schools and one university in its main industrial area, although residents seeking specialized education often leave the Zone. Fixing is also particularly common. Rho's isolation and limited law-enforcement coverage make it a common starting point and temporary base for Fixers. SUBZONES / DISTRICTS Industrial District Rho's primary administrative and industrial center. It contains the largest concentration of Monolith offices, corporate infrastructure, major water facilities, and industrial employment, along with a relatively small city. Badlands District The largest and least-developed part of Rho. It consists primarily of barren wilderness, abandoned infrastructure, remote roads, isolated water sources, mines, workshops, and scattered settlements. Monolith services and Gavel presence are more limited here. Historical District The districts containing Rho's established towns and communities, including older settlements and newer communities built around industrial facilities. KEY LOCATIONS The Industrial District: Rho's largest concentration of corporate infrastructure, industry, businesses, and employment. Major Water Facilities: Large extraction, purification, storage, and distribution complexes operated by AquaFlo. Frontier Towns: Numerous small settlements spread throughout the Zone. Dustball Grounds: Local and regional sporting grounds found throughout the Zone. Racing Grounds: Organized tracks and open areas used for professional and amateur racing. ECONOMY Water extraction and distribution form the foundation of Rho's economy. AquaFlo operates the majority of the Zone's large-scale water infrastructure and supplies water to other Zones. Other industries include mining, quarrying, construction, transportation, freight, salvage, fabrication, repair, and other trades. Economic conditions vary considerably between communities. Areas connected to major industrial operations generally have better infrastructure and employment opportunities, while remote settlements have fewer services and greater dependence on local resources. Despite Rho's economic importance to Zenith, poverty and inequality remain widespread. CREATING A RHOAN CHARACTER A character from Rho could come from a small frontier settlement, an industrial company town, or one of the Zone's larger communities. Common backgrounds include water-industry workers, mechanics, racers, tradespeople, Fixers, and people involved in local businesses. Rhoans are often familiar with long-distance travel, vehicle maintenance, practical repair work, and making do with limited resources. Someone from a wealthier or more urban Zone may find Rho's culture old-fashioned, while a Rhoan may see those same people as sheltered or overly dependent on corporate infrastructure. TRIVIA Rho is the largest source of processed water for the rest of Zenith. Vehicle and racing programs frequently use Rho as a filming location because of its open terrain. Some Rhoan communities maintain buildings and machinery that have been repaired or modified for generations. Locally produced alcohol is often considered unusually strong by people from other Zones. Rho's major annual festival has historically remained independent of Monolith sponsorship. Rhoans generally have a higher degree of practical mechanical and self-sufficiency skills than outsiders.

title: What is Retrograde?
text: RETROGRADE is a science-fiction setting, set nearly a thousand years after Earth was abandoned due to global warming. Eventually through their travels, humanity found a new home on Planet Zenith . Welcome to Zenith! Zenith is divided into 24 Zones, large protected territories where most of humanity lives. Between the Zones lies the Pale, a dangerous and largely uninhabitable region. Zenith is highly advanced, but its design and everyday use often resemble older technology. Physical media, cartridges, specialized computers, and chunky personal devices remain common alongside highly advanced infrastructure. For more information on Zenith, check Zenith The Monoliths Each Zone is controlled by one of 24 Monoliths. Monoliths are enormous corporations that also function as governments. They control the land, infrastructure, resources, and administration of their Zones. Though not elected, and each Monolith is ruled by its own leadership. The Monoliths compete with one another, but they also depend heavily on one another. Together, they form The Conglomerate, the collective government in a shaky alliance, responsible for matters affecting all of Zenith. For a list of Monoliths check Organizations Life on Zenith Most people live relatively ordinary lives. They go to school, work, shop, eat, travel, use the internet, and live in cities much like people have for centuries. Life, however, varies greatly depending on where someone lives and how much money they have. Wealthier people have access to better housing, food, education, healthcare, and employment, while poorer people may live in overcrowded areas with fewer opportunities. If you have a specific question about Zenith’s daily life, its likely answered in Society Fixers Fixers are independent contractors who provide specialized services to private individuals, organizations, and Corporations. Unlike boring corpo employees, Fixers are (generally) self-employed and are hired on a job by job basis to solve problems that a client cannot or doesn't want to handle themselves. A Fixer's work may be entirely legal, highly illegal, or somewhere in between depending on the client, zone, and circumstances. Fixer groups are called Networks. Your first Retrograde character will likely belong to a Fixer group known as The Enclave . This is to help your character connect with others, get jobs, money, and other opportunities. Signatures Very rarely, a person may be chosen by a Signature. Signatures are extraordinarily powerful anomalous weapons that bind themselves to a specific person. They cannot simply be picked up and used by someone else. A Signature grants its wielder unusual abilities, making its users exceptionally powerful and often dangerous. Very little is known about where Signatures came from or why they choose the people they do. For more information, refer to Signatures Project Identity Despite its themes, Retrograde is not cyberpunk. Instead, Retrograde has a distinct Cassette Futurist aesthetic. Its technology is advanced, but it often looks and feels like an imagined future from decades ago. As a project, it is intended to feel Bizarre, Colorful, Brutalist, “Street,” Corporate, and Darkly Comedic. Okay, but what is Retrograde actually about? There is no single dominant story taking place in Zenith. It is a world designed to contain many different stories, characters, and places. All in all, It can be about whatever you make it to be. But if you want more of an answer, its about people learning to thrive in a world where every aspect of reality wants you dead. Where do I go next? To see a list of Zones, check ZONES And to read random worldbuilding bits about the general functioning and society of Zenith, check Society
